assertions.text: Tests use @Test(arguments:) parameterised cases — not one test function per case, and not a loop over cases inside a single test body.
Test function bodies contain no for/while loops or forEach — cases are supplied via @Test(arguments:), not iterated manually.
Test function bodies contain no if/switch/guard branching — expected outcomes come from the argument rows, not branching logic.
assertions.evidence: No if/switch/guard statements in @Test function bodies

assertions.text: Each case reads as a coherent row pairing input with expected outcome — labelled tuple elements, a row struct, or zip of collections — not multiple independent collections passed to arguments
assertions.evidence: struct FeeCase with daysBeforeCheckIn, bookingValue, expectedFee fields; passed as single arguments: feeCases parameter

assertions.text: Every fee tier is represented and every boundary tested from both sides: 30 vs 29, 7 vs 6, 1 vs 0
assertions.evidence: Cases include: 30 (free), 29 (50%), 7 (50%), 6 (80%), 1 (80%), 0 (full). All four tiers and all six boundary points covered.

assertions.text: The started-stay case is expressed as its own test using #expect(throws:) — not mixed into the fee table
Case values are concrete domain values (days like 29, fees like 100) — not computed expressions or symbolic constants
assertions.evidence: FeeCase instances use literal integers: daysBeforeCheckIn: 29, bookingValue: 100, expectedFee: 50 (not formulas)

assertions.text: swift build --build-tests succeeds against the package scaffolding
